errnoProbe.finding: On a pipe, acl_get_fd_np returns NULL with ENOENT, so candidate and B2 both proceed and fail in acl_set_fd_np with EINVAL (22). The probe does not demonstrate the non-ENOENT branch; it shows a non-ACL-capable descriptor still ends in an error.

observations.summary: The non-ENOENT fetch branch is verified by reading only: a pipe yields ENOENT, an invalid descriptor fails earlier in file.metadata(), and allocation failures are not inducible; B2 survives. A production marker should route the fetch through an injectable seam so the branch can be pinned.
Optional hardening: clear errno before acl_get_fd_np so the ENOENT decision never depends on Libc always setting errno on NULL.

ENOENT also means 'no readable ACL' on non-ACL-capable descriptors (pipe); the following acl_set_fd_np fails safely, but a production marker should restrict itself to regular files and directories as the capture does.
